subtitle: 我娘不是省油的灯
sentences: I had thought that once the authorities sealed our accounting office, some of the shop workers would start packing their things the very next day.
Instead, before dawn had even broken, Mother hauled me out of bed.
"Put your shoes on. Front courtyard."
"Mother, even the roosters aren't awake yet."
"They've crowed twice. You slept through both. If you don't get up, I'll deduct Chuntao's wages and put the blame on you."
Chuntao was standing outside the door. "Madam," she ventured, "Miss stayed up half the night memorizing the names of the shipping firms."
Mother gave me a look. "How many can you name?"
"Six!" I blurted out.
"There are seven."
"...What was the last family's surname again?"
Madam Li turned on her heel and walked away. I had no choice but to throw on an outer robe and hurry after her.

A dozen or more lamps lit the front courtyard. Uncle Qin and the managers from our various shops stood around a long table piled high with contracts, samples, and abacuses. The salt merchant who had been weeping about closing up shop the night before was now arguing with the cloth-shop manager over a delivery note.
"That cart belongs to the salt business!"
"The carriage contract says it belongs to the cloth shop!"
"Who controls the cart doesn't matter! If we don't sell the salt today, we might as well let it take a bath in the rain!"
I was just getting interested when Mother tapped the tabletop with an abacus.

"Enough. The authorities sealed the accounts connected with the old North River case, not every shop the Jiang family owns. If I hear anyone spreading the story that the whole business has been shut down, bring him back here and teach him to read."
She spread four documents across the table.

The first was the prefectural office's inventory of sealed property, listing the old ledgers, cargo tickets, and cabinets no one was allowed to move. The second showed our scheduled sailings. The third listed the wages owed to more than fifty workers this month. The fourth was the thinnest of all, but Mother lingered over it longer than the rest.
I leaned over. "What's this one?"
"Someone wants their loan repaid ahead of schedule."
"But isn't it due next month?"
"The contract clearly says that if Jiang Trading House becomes involved in a legal dispute, the lender may demand early repayment."
"Surely they'd have to prove we're guilty first?"
Mother tapped one character with her fingertip: involved.
"It says involved, not convicted. When you read a contract, you look at how much we borrowed and miss a line like this."

I sat down without another word. Before getting transported into this novel, I hadn't even understood the automatic-renewal clause on my gym membership. And here I'd nearly volunteered to run a trading house in ancient times.

Mother turned to Uncle Qin. "Send the three carts of cloth from the western warehouse as agreed. If the salt can go by road, supply the nearby restaurants first. Touch nothing on the sealed-property list. If anyone so much as lays a finger on the lock of the old accounting room, I'll hand him over to the authorities myself."
I asked, "Could the officials seize today's shipments too?"

"They could," she said. "Which is why we must explain exactly which shipments have nothing to do with the old case—and find someone willing to vouch for us. Who is going to believe us just because we say, 'We didn't do it'?"
She handed me a calling card.
"Today you'll meet Chairman Jiang of the merchants' guild."
My eyes lit up. "You're finally letting me negotiate a business deal?"
"You're going to listen."
"Listen to what?"
"How much he dares to demand. Don't agree to anything. Uncle Qin will take notes for you."
I accepted the card and turned it over. My escorts were listed on the back: Chuntao, Uncle Qin, two accounting clerks, and Second Aunt.
"Mother, am I going to discuss business or face execution?"
"A bride escaped on your watch a few days ago," she said without changing expression. "I don't want a shop escaping today as well."
Chuntao lowered her head to fuss with the bags, her shoulders shaking so hard she could barely keep still.
Chairman Jiang was watering two pots of crabapple blossoms when we arrived.
He greeted us with a kindly smile, invited Second Aunt to the seat of honor, and remarked that I looked just as I had when I was little. Before I could be touched, he heaved a sigh.
"I understand the Jiang family's difficulties. But now that you're involved in a lawsuit, the guild can't speak up for you lightly. The other shopkeepers would object."

Uncle Qin presented the list we had prepared. "We're asking the chairman to act as a witness, nothing more. Jiang Trading House is willing to have the prefectural office inspect the goods unrelated to the case separately. Guild members know who owns each shipment and where it is headed. They can attest to those facts."
"A witness? Of course." Chairman Jiang set the list aside. "But you have debts to pay, goods piling up, and no guarantee that business will improve."
I could tell he wasn't finished.
Sure enough, he pulled another sheet of paper from beneath a flower stand.
"If you'd transfer your two shops on East Street into my nephew's name, we could talk about the price. With silver in hand, why worry about cash flow?"
I took one look and nearly burst out laughing.
The rent from those two shops last year alone had been considerably higher than the total sum he was offering.
"Master Jiang," I said, looking up, "is your nephew buying the shops, or buying my mother's life?"
Second Aunt immediately coughed. I swallowed my next remark and tried again. "Sorry. I don't know much about business. The price just seems rather far off."
Chairman Jiang's smile thinned. "Young ladies do speak their minds. But who else is willing to pay you anything right now?"
"Whether anyone can pay is something we'll work out at home." I pushed the paper back. "If you can witness the shipments, we'd be grateful. If not, let's say we came to admire your flowers."
He slowly closed his account book. "Do you know who's been asking about the value of the Jiang family's shops lately?"
"Your nephew?"
"Besides my nephew, a steward from the Xie residence."
My smile froze.
Chairman Jiang finally told the truth. "The heir sent someone to ask how many more days your family could hold out. If that marriage connection can still be salvaged, why make an enemy of them?"
So that was what this was about.
I glanced at Uncle Qin. He said nothing, merely slid the transfer agreement Chairman Jiang had been holding down back across the table.

"Chairman," Uncle Qin said, "Jiang Trading House has not stopped delivering goods or fallen behind on its guild dues. We are requesting only an endorsement confirming the trade dealings you know to be true. We are not asking the guild to authorize the release of any goods on the prefecture's behalf. If that's inconvenient, we'll ask two established merchants who shared shipping routes with us back then."
Chairman Jiang's hand went still.
Before I could react, Second Aunt chimed in. "Exactly. I remember which families borrowed Jiang boats when the river froze at Dongping Wharf. Surely that old goodwill still counts for something."
Chairman Jiang fell silent for a while, then picked up our shipment list again.
"I'll sign only for what I've verified myself," he said. "Two sailing dates and one former cargo owner. You'll have to find other witnesses for the rest."
"That's enough," Uncle Qin said. "We won't ask you to put your name to anything you can't stand behind. Thank you, Chairman."
I wasn't satisfied. "That's enough?"
As we left, Second Aunt rapped me lightly with her folding fan.
"You were about to start insulting him again, weren't you?"
"At that price, we'd make more money tearing the doors off the shops and selling the timber!"

"All the more reason not to insult him." Uncle Qin tucked the endorsement away. "His signature on the part he handled gives us a chance to request shipment-by-shipment inspections from the prefecture. Only the officials can decide whether the goods may leave. If you'd overturned the table, we wouldn't even have this piece of paper."
I stared at the document in his hand. At last, I was beginning to understand why Mother had sent me to listen.
She hadn't expected me to win everything in one sitting.
She wanted me to learn that some people would rather help you as little as possible than miss a chance to take advantage of you.

By the time we returned home that evening, the salt-shop manager had obtained a receipt showing that one batch of goods unrelated to the case had been inspected. Whether the carts could leave tomorrow was still uncertain, but at least we no longer had to gamble on moving the goods in secret.
Mother didn't so much as raise an eyebrow when she heard Chairman Jiang's offer.
"Even lower than I expected."
"You knew he'd try something like that?"

"I knew he wanted to buy the shops. I didn't know how low he'd dare to go." She had Uncle Qin record the amount. "When we do business with the Jiang guild chairman next month, remember to charge a higher rate."
It suddenly struck me that Xie Linzhou had picked the wrong family to bully.
But halfway through smiling, I remembered what Mother had said the night before.
"Mother, those old accounts you showed me a few days ago..."
I stopped. Suddenly I wasn't sure I wanted to ask.
Mother looked up. "You want to know about the entry marked 'additional'?"
I nodded. "What was it really for?"
Her hand stopped moving over the abacus.
Mother told Chuntao to shut the doors. Only when the courtyard had emptied and the two of us were alone did she take a receipt from her sleeve, its folds worn nearly white.
"Two hundred taels," she said. "Three years ago, Steward Zhao—the man overseeing the grain shipments—had someone bring it to me."
I examined the receipt. The payment seal was genuine. Accountant Song had entered the transaction, and the words "additional transport wages" were written beside it.
"Why an additional payment?"

"They wanted me to issue another delivery receipt, change the date to the ninth day of the twelfth lunar month, and state that the Jiang boats had delivered the entire shipment to the North River government granary."
"Did you change it?"
"No." Her answer came at once. Then she lowered her eyes. "I didn't change it. But I took the money."
I went blank.
"Then you should have sent it back!"
"At the time, I thought that if I accepted it, they would stop harassing Accountant Song and the boatmen."
"And what happened?"

"They produced other documents themselves. Accountant Song wanted to report it, and I stopped him. The two hundred taels have remained in our private accounts ever since. Not a single coin has been touched."
Her voice was steady, but the fingers gripping the receipt had gone white.

"I didn't make a false delivery receipt," she said, meeting my eyes. "But I knew someone intended to. I accepted their money, failed to report them, and even stopped Accountant Song from speaking out. If you ask whether our family is blameless, I can't tell you it is."
I wanted to say she'd only been trying to protect our family.
But the words died on my lips.
If five thousand shi of grain really had been taken that year, how many people had been counting on it to survive the winter? I didn't know.
Those two hundred taels were still sitting there, like a stone too hot for anyone to touch.
"Does Wen Li know?" I asked.
"No. Not from me, at any rate."
"Then what am I supposed to do?"
Mother pushed the receipt toward me.

"You promised to investigate with her, so tell her what she deserves to know. Tomorrow I'll see Gu Huaichuan and give him a truthful account of the payment, along with this receipt. Whether I'm fined or investigated, I won't wait for the Xie family to bring it out and use it against me."
I looked from the receipt to her face.
"Mother, aren't you afraid?"
"I am," she said. "But today made one thing clear. The Xie family has no intention of letting us live in peace. If I keep hiding this, I'll only be giving them a handhold on my throat."
I folded the paper and handed it back.
"Then I'll go with you tomorrow."
Mother gave me a look. "Eat first."
"You're not going to scold me?"
"Would it do any good?"
"Every now and then. A little."
"Then if you oversleep again tomorrow, I'll keep scolding you."
I couldn't manage a laugh. I simply reached out and hugged her.
Mother stiffened for a moment, then patted me on the back.
"That's enough hugging. It's hot. Go wash your hands."
She was still finding fault with me, as usual. But I could hear that some of the tension had finally left her voice.
That night, for the first time, I wasn't thinking about the fire in Chapter Nineteen.
Only one thought filled my head: how was I supposed to tell Wen Li tomorrow that Mother really had accepted those two hundred taels?
translations: 我以为铺子被封账房以后，第二天就该有伙计卷铺盖走人。
结果天还没亮，我娘先把我从床上拎了起来。
“穿鞋。去前院。”
“娘，鸡都没叫。”
“鸡叫了两遍，你没听见。再不起，我把春桃的月钱扣到你头上。”
春桃就在门外，闻言小声说：“夫人，小姐睡前背了半夜船行的名字。”
我娘看我一眼：“背出几个？”
“六个！”我抢答。
“总共七个。”
“……还有一个姓什么来着？”
李氏转身就走。我只好披着外衫追出去。
前院点了十几盏灯。秦叔带着各铺掌柜站成一圈，中间的长桌堆满了契书、货样和算盘。昨夜还哭着说要散伙的盐货掌柜，此刻正跟布行的人争一张货单。
“这是盐货走的车！”
“车契写的是布行！”
“车归谁管不重要，车上的盐今天再不卖，就该进雨水里泡澡了！”
我正听得起劲，李氏用算盘敲了敲桌面。
“都别吵。官府封的是北河旧案相关账房，不是姜家所有铺面。谁再在外头说姜记全被封了，先把他带回来认字。”
她把四份文书摊开。
一份是府衙封存清单，写着不得挪动的旧账、货票和柜子；一份是原本约好的船期；另一份列着这月该发给五十余名伙计的工钱；最后一份最薄，却叫她多看了好几眼。
我凑过去：“这是什么？”
“有人要提前收回借款。”
“可不是下个月才到期？”
“契上写得清楚，姜记若涉官司，对方便可提前催还。”
“那也得等查出咱家有罪吧？”
母亲用指尖点了点“涉”字。
“人家写的是涉，不是定罪。你看契的时候只看借了多少，没看还有这一行。”
我老老实实坐下。穿书前我连健身房自动续费都没看明白，差点真在古代替人经营商号。
李氏转向秦叔：“西仓那三车布按原约发。盐货若能走陆路，就先送近处酒楼。封存清单里的东西一概不动。谁敢去碰旧账房的锁，我先送他进官府。”
我问：“官府会不会连今天发的货也扣住？”
“有可能。”她说，“所以要把哪一批货与旧案无关讲清楚，还要有人替我们作保。光说‘我没有’谁信？”
她递给我一张拜帖。
“今日去见商会蒋会首。”
我眼睛一亮：“终于让我出门谈生意了？”
“你去听。”
“听什么？”
“听他开多大的口。话先别接，秦叔替你记。”
我接过帖子，翻到背面。陪同的人写了春桃、秦叔、两名账房伙计，另有二姑母。
“娘，您这是让我谈生意，还是让我去上刑场？”
“前几天刚有个新娘从你手里跑了。”她面无表情，“我怕今日再跑一间铺子。”
春桃低头去整理包袱，肩膀抖得像筛糠。
蒋会首见我们时，正在给两盆海棠浇水。
他满面慈祥，请二姑母坐上首，又夸我长得像小时候。我还没来得及感动，他便叹起气来。
“姜家的难处，我是知道的。如今有官司，商会若轻易替你们说话，别家掌柜也不服啊。”
秦叔把备好的清单呈上去：“今日求会首做的是见证。姜记愿意让府衙另验非涉案货物，商会中有人熟悉每批货的货主和去向，可以替我们说明。”
“见证自然能做。”蒋会首把清单放到一边，“只是你们现在欠账多，货压着，往后生意未必好做。”
我一听，就知道后面还有话。
果然，他从花架底下取出另一份纸。
“东街两处铺面，若肯转到我侄儿名下，价格好商量。拿了现银，还愁什么周转？”
我接过一看，险些笑出声。
两间铺子光是去年的租金，就比他开出的总价高不少。
“蒋老爷，”我抬头，“您侄儿买的是铺面，还是我娘的命？”
二姑母立刻咳了一声。我咽回下一句，改口：“抱歉，我不懂生意，只觉得这价差得有点远。”
蒋会首笑容淡了：“小姑娘心直口快。可眼下谁还肯出钱？”
“出不出得了钱，我们回去再算。”我把纸推回去，“您若能帮忙做个货物见证，我们感激。若是不能，今日就当来给您看花。”
他慢慢合上账本：“你知道最近是谁在问姜家铺面的价吗？”
“您侄儿？”
“除了我侄儿，还有谢府的管事。”
我嘴角一僵。
蒋会首看着我，终于说了句实话：“世子派人来问过我，姜家还撑得住几日。你们那门亲若还能认，何必把关系闹僵？”
原来是这么回事。
我看了一眼秦叔。他没有说话，只把蒋会首用手压住的那张转让纸轻轻推回桌上。
“会首，”秦叔说，“姜记尚未断货，也未拖欠行会公摊。今日所求只是一份见证商号往来事实的签注，不请商会替府衙放行。若贵会不便，我们去请当年共同走船的两家老行商。”
蒋会首的手停住了。
我还没反应过来，二姑母便接话：“对。当年东平码头遇上冻河，姜记借过船给哪几家，我可都记得。这点情面总还在。”
蒋会首沉默了一会儿，重新拿起姜家的货单。
“我只能签我亲眼核过的部分。”他说，“两处船期、一个旧货主，剩下的你们自己找人。”
“够了。”秦叔说，“谁的名字也不白担着。辛苦会首。”
我有些不甘心：“这就够了？”
出门时，二姑母拿扇子敲了我一下。
“刚才差点又想骂人是不是？”
“他开那个价，铺子的门板拆了卖木头都比他给得多！”
“所以更不能骂。”秦叔把签注收好，“他肯写自己经手的那部分，算是让我们有机会再向府衙申请逐批核验。但真正能不能出货，还得官府核。若你把桌子掀了，连这张纸都没有。”
我看着他手里的纸，终于有点明白我娘为什么让我来听。
不是让我今天赢一大场。
是让我知道，有些人宁可少帮你一点，也不会错过趁机占便宜。
傍晚回府，盐货掌柜已经拿到一份非涉案货物的验看回执。明天能否发车还未定，至少不必靠偷偷搬货赌运气。
李氏听完蒋家的报价，连眉毛都没动一下。
“果然比我猜的还低。”
“您知道他会这样？”
“我知道他想买，却不知道他敢开多低。”她让秦叔把数目记下，“下个月和蒋家做生意，利钱记得往上算。”
我忽然觉得谢临舟挑错了软柿子。
可笑到一半，我想起她昨晚说过的话。
“娘，前几天您拿给我看的旧账……”
话说到一半，我又有点不敢问。
李氏抬眼：“你想问那个‘另’字？”
我点头：“到底是什么？”
她手里的算盘停了。
母亲吩咐春桃关门，等院里只剩我们两个，才从袖中取出一张折得发白的收银存单。
“两百两。”她说，“三年前，那位经手粮运的赵管事让人送来的。”
我看着单据。收款印是真的，记账的是宋账房，旁边还写着“另付脚钱”。
“为什么另付？”
“他们想让我补一份运粮回执，日期改成腊月初九，写姜记的船如数送到了北河官仓。”
“您改了？”
“没有。”她答得很快，随后却低下眼，“我没改。但钱我收了。”
我愣住。
“那您退回去啊。”
“我当时想，收下了，他们就不会再找宋账房和船工的麻烦。”
“结果呢？”
“结果他们自己弄出了别的单据。宋账房想去告，我拦了他。那两百两一直记在私账里，一分也没动。”
她说得很平静，只有握着存单的指头在发白。
“我没做假回执。”她看着我，“可我知道有人要做假，收了钱，没报官，还拦过宋账房。你若问姜家干不干净，我不能答你干净。”
我想说，她也是为了护住家里人。
但话到了嘴边，没说出来。
那年要是真有五千石粮被人拿走，多少人靠着那些粮过冬？我不知道。
两百两现在躺在这里，倒像一块谁也不敢动的烫石头。
“这事温梨知道吗？”我问。
“不知道。至少我没告诉她。”
“那我怎么办？”
母亲将存单推到我手边。
“你既然答应跟她一起查，就把你该说的告诉她。明日我去见顾怀川，先把这笔钱和存单如实交代。是罚是查，不能等谢家拿出来替我说。”
我看了看存单，又看向她。
“娘，您不怕？”
“怕。”她说，“不过今天我看明白了。谢家不打算让我们平平安安把日子过下去。再藏着，只会叫人抓住脖子。”
我把纸折好，还给她。
“那明日我陪您去。”
李氏看我一眼：“先吃饭。”
“您不骂我？”
“骂你管用？”
“偶尔管一点。”
“那你明早再起晚，我就继续骂。”
我笑不出来，只伸手去抱她。
母亲僵了僵，最后拍了拍我的后背。
“别抱了，热。去把手洗了。”
她照旧嫌弃我，可我听得出来，她那口气终于松了一点。
这一夜，我第一次没有想着第十九章的大火。
满脑子都是另一件事：明天该怎样告诉温梨，我娘真的收过那两百两。

annotations.explain: once在此引导时间从句，表示某事发生后随即出现的结果；不是“曾经”。
annotations.example: Once the report is signed, we can send it.

annotations.explain: pack one's things 是常见生活表达，可暗示辞职、搬走或结束停留。
annotations.example: He packed his things and left the office.

annotations.explain: dawn breaks 是固定的文学化说法；even 强调行动发生得异常早。
annotations.example: We set off before dawn had broken.

annotations.explain: haul someone out of bed 比 wake up 强调费力或不情愿，适合表现母亲的强势。
annotations.example: Dad hauled us out of bed at six.

annotations.explain: put on 强调穿戴动作，wear 强调已穿戴的状态。
annotations.example: Put your coat on before going outside.

annotations.phrase: even the roosters aren't awake yet
annotations.explain: even 用于引出极端例子，突出时间太早；这是夸张的抱怨口吻。
annotations.example: Even the shops aren't open yet.

annotations.explain: sleep through something 表示睡得太沉，整个响声或事件都没把人吵醒。
annotations.example: I slept through the alarm.

annotations.explain: deduct ... from ... 表示从总额中扣除；wages 常指按时或按工作支付的工资。
annotations.example: They deducted the fee from my pay.

annotations.explain: put the blame on somebody 是常见固定表达，和 blame somebody for something 搭配相近。
annotations.example: Don't put the blame on your sister.

annotations.explain: venture to say/ask 在叙事中表示明知可能冒犯，仍试着发言；不指旅行冒险。
annotations.example: She ventured a question during the meeting.

annotations.explain: stay up 表示熬夜不睡；half the night 是持续时间状语，不一定精确六小时。
annotations.example: I stayed up half the night studying.

annotations.explain: give somebody a look 往往暗示警告、怀疑或不赞成，要结合后文判断。
annotations.example: She gave me a look when I interrupted.

annotations.explain: blurt out 指没来得及思考就突然说出来，可接回答或秘密。
annotations.example: He blurted out the answer.

annotations.explain: 句尾 again 在口语中可用于回忆忘记的信息，并非真的重复动作。
annotations.example: What was her name again?

annotations.explain: turn on one's heel 是描写迅速、决绝转身的惯用表达。
annotations.example: She turned on her heel and marched away.

annotations.explain: have no choice but to do sth 是固定句型，but 后接不定式。
annotations.example: We had no choice but to wait.

annotations.explain: throw on 表示随手、匆忙穿上；和字面“扔”不同。
annotations.example: I threw on a jacket and ran outside.

annotations.explain: be piled high with 常描写物品堆得很高，重在画面感。
annotations.example: The desk was piled high with books.

annotations.explain: close up shop 可指实体店打烊，也可泛指停止经营某件事。
annotations.example: After twenty years, they closed up shop.

annotations.explain: argue with somebody over/about something 是标准搭配；with 后面是争论对象。
annotations.example: They argued over the final bill.

annotations.explain: might as well 常表示在不理想的情况下干脆做某事，带无奈或讽刺。
annotations.example: It's raining, so we might as well stay home.

annotations.phrase: take a bath in the rain
annotations.explain: 把盐“洗澡”是夸张拟人说法，写出了老板焦急的吐槽，不能机械理解为实际洗澡。
annotations.example: My shoes got a bath in the rain.

annotations.explain: be getting + 形容词 表示状态渐渐发生变化；这里讲故事叙事中的“刚开始”。
annotations.example: The conversation was getting interesting.

annotations.explain: tap 表示轻敲，和 knock/bang 相比动作更轻，常用来提醒别人注意。
annotations.example: She tapped the desk with her pen.

annotations.explain: spread a story/rumor 是常见搭配，不保证故事的真实性。
annotations.example: Someone has been spreading rumors.

annotations.explain: shut down 比 close 更强调停止运作，适用于企业、系统或机构。
annotations.example: The factory was shut down for repairs.

annotations.explain: 此处不是普通教学请求，而是李氏讽刺别人不识公告内容、乱传消息。
annotations.example: Read the notice before you complain.

annotations.explain: spread ... across ... 表示将东西展开铺在某平面上；不同于传播传言的 spread。
annotations.example: She spread the maps across the floor.

annotations.explain: 现在分词 listing 补充说明清单的内容，可理解为 which listed。
annotations.example: He handed over a report listing the costs.

annotations.phrase: no one was allowed to move
annotations.explain: be allowed to do 表示得到许可；这里是被动式加否定，表示禁令。
annotations.example: Visitors are not allowed to enter.

annotations.explain: linger over 可指目光停留、慢慢品味或反复考虑，具有文学叙事色彩。
annotations.example: She lingered over the last paragraph.

annotations.explain: lean over 指身体前倾去看或够某物，不是移动住所。
annotations.example: He leaned over to read the label.

annotations.explain: ahead of schedule 是很常用的时间表达，可用于提前还款、交付或完工。
annotations.example: We finished the project ahead of schedule.

annotations.explain: be due 表示款项到期、任务应完成或某事预计发生，取义看上下文。
annotations.example: The payment is due on Friday.

annotations.explain: be involved in 强调与事情有联系，不等于已被证明有罪。
annotations.example: Her firm became involved in a dispute.

annotations.explain: demand 与 request 相比更强硬；repayment 是偿还已借款项。
annotations.example: The bank demanded early repayment.

annotations.explain: would have to 在此表示说话人推断的应然条件，不是真正有权决定规则。
annotations.example: They'd have to show some evidence first.

annotations.explain: guilty 是法律或道德意义上的有罪；与 merely involved 的区分是本段关键。
annotations.example: Being questioned doesn't make you guilty.

annotations.explain: with + 工具或身体部位 表示动作凭借的方式；这里 with her fingertip 修饰 tap。
annotations.example: He traced the line with his finger.

annotations.explain: be convicted of 指经法律程序被判有罪；和涉案 be involved in 不同。
annotations.example: He was charged but never convicted.

annotations.explain: miss 可表示错过、遗漏注意到某内容，不一定是想念。
annotations.example: I missed the small print.

annotations.explain: without another word 常用于被驳倒、气馁或愤怒后的动作衔接。
annotations.example: She left without another word.

annotations.explain: clause 是合同中的具体条款；这句现代健身房类比突出穿书者的吐槽。
annotations.example: Check the renewal clause before signing.

annotations.explain: nearly 表示差点发生但实际没有；volunteer to 指自愿做某事。
annotations.example: I nearly volunteered to organize everything.

annotations.explain: as agreed 是固定的省略表达，相当于 as we previously agreed。
annotations.example: We'll deliver the goods as agreed.

annotations.explain: by road/by sea/by rail 可表示运输或出行方式，不用冠词。
annotations.example: These goods will go by road.

annotations.phrase: so much as lays a finger on
annotations.explain: not/if ... so much as ... 用于强调连最小动作也不许；lay a finger on 为碰触的惯用表达。
annotations.example: If anyone so much as touches it, tell me.

annotations.explain: hand over someone/something to someone 是移交的常见搭配。
annotations.example: They handed the documents over to police.

annotations.explain: seize 在执法语境中指依法或强制扣押，强于 take。
annotations.example: Officials seized the shipment.

annotations.explain: Which is why... 承接前句原因，口语与叙事都常用，是句间连接表达。
annotations.example: The roads are closed, which is why we're late.

annotations.explain: have nothing to do with 是高频固定搭配，反义可说 have something to do with。
annotations.example: This has nothing to do with me.

annotations.explain: vouch for 通常表示基于自己的了解保证某人或事实可信，不等于具有行政审批权。
annotations.example: I can vouch for her honesty.

annotations.explain: just because 引导原因，常见于反问或否定句，表示“不能仅仅因为”。
annotations.example: It's not true just because he says so.

annotations.explain: calling card 在历史语境可指拜访时递送的名帖，与现代电话卡无关。
annotations.example: He sent a calling card ahead of his visit.

annotations.explain: one's eyes light up 表示突然兴奋、感兴趣，属于常见情绪描写。
annotations.example: Her eyes lit up at the news.

annotations.explain: be going to 在此表达安排或命令，而不是预测天气类未来。
annotations.example: You're going to sit here and listen.

annotations.explain: dare to + 动词表示敢于做某事；这句话暗含母亲早就预料对方会趁火打劫。
annotations.example: How much would they dare to charge?

annotations.explain: agree to something 表示接受提议、条件；agree with somebody 表示认同某人。
annotations.example: Don't agree to a deal yet.

annotations.explain: turn over 用于把物体翻面；这里 it 指 calling card，不是“移交”。
annotations.example: Turn the sheet over to read the back.

annotations.explain: be listed 表示被列在名单中；on the back 表示纸张背面。
annotations.example: The instructions are listed on the back.

annotations.explain: face 常与困难、风险或惩罚连用：face a problem/trial；这里是夸张玩笑。
annotations.example: He might face a heavy fine.

annotations.explain: on someone's watch 是固定习语，表示某人值守或负责期间发生了事情。
annotations.example: That mistake happened on my watch.

annotations.explain: without + doing 或名词短语说明伴随状态，强调说话者冷静。
annotations.example: She listened without changing expression.

annotations.explain: fuss with 表示反复整理、摆弄小事；这里是春桃掩饰偷笑。
annotations.example: He fussed with his tie before speaking.

annotations.explain: 名词 + 现在分词可形成独立主格/伴随结构，突出同时发生的动作。
annotations.example: She sat quietly, her hands trembling.

annotations.explain: crabapple 为海棠类苹果属观赏花木，作为场景植物营造人物表面从容。
annotations.example: The crabapple tree bloomed in spring.

annotations.explain: seat of honor 指礼仪上安排给贵宾的重要位置，有社交等级含义。
annotations.example: They offered the guest the seat of honor.

annotations.explain: before I could ... 表示某反应尚未发生就被打断；touched 在此指受到感动。
annotations.example: Before I could reply, she had left.

annotations.explain: heave a sigh 比 sigh 更形象，突出有意或夸张地叹气。
annotations.example: He heaved a sigh of relief.

annotations.explain: speak up for someone 表示公开支持或辩护；与 speak up（大声说）相关但意义更具体。
annotations.example: She spoke up for her colleague.

annotations.explain: would 在此表示假设情况下可能的反应，object 常与 to + 名词/动名词连用。
annotations.example: The neighbors would object to the noise.

annotations.explain: present 在正式场合可以表示呈交文件、陈述材料，不只是介绍人。
annotations.example: She presented the evidence to the judge.

annotations.explain: act as 表示担任某种角色，不意味着有官府批准权限。
annotations.example: Can you act as our witness?

annotations.explain: nothing more 用于缩小要求范围、消除他人的顾虑。
annotations.example: It's a preliminary review, nothing more.

annotations.explain: attest to 是正式书面用语，意为基于见闻证实某事。
annotations.example: The records attest to the shipment dates.

annotations.explain: set aside 可指暂时放下某物，也可指预留资源、搁置分歧，需看宾语。
annotations.example: Let's set that issue aside for now.

annotations.explain: pile up 作不及物短语动词，表示逐渐堆积，常用于工作、债务和库存。
annotations.example: Orders are piling up.

annotations.explain: there is no guarantee that ... 是常用判断句型，that 后接完整从句。
annotations.example: There's no guarantee that it'll work.

annotations.explain: not be finished 可表示动作未完成，这里透出“还有条件”的预感。
annotations.example: He isn't finished explaining yet.

annotations.explain: sure enough 常用于事态印证此前预感，不等于简单的“当然”。
annotations.example: Sure enough, it started raining.

annotations.explain: beneath 既可表示物理位置，也可用于文雅叙述。
annotations.example: She pulled a box from beneath the bed.

annotations.explain: transfer 在法律和商业语境指转移资产、权利或所有权；后续合同须看具体条款。
annotations.example: They transferred the property to their son.

annotations.explain: in someone's name 表示归属或登记名义，转入某人名下常说 into someone's name。
annotations.example: The car is registered in her name.

annotations.explain: with + 名词 + 介词短语说明具备某种条件；cash in hand 是现代常用表达。
annotations.example: With cash in hand, they could reopen.

annotations.explain: cash flow 指资金流入流出及周转能力，不等同于盈利。
annotations.example: The company has a cash-flow problem.

annotations.explain: burst out laughing 是固定结构，强调突然忍不住笑；nearly 表示最终忍住。
annotations.example: I nearly burst out laughing at the joke.

annotations.explain: alone 放在数量或名词后表示“仅这一项就”，强调对比。
annotations.example: The rent alone costs a fortune.

annotations.explain: considerably 修饰比较级，表示差距相当大，比 a bit 高得多。
annotations.example: Costs were considerably higher than expected.

annotations.explain: or 在反问里给出夸张的对立选项，实际指压价近乎落井下石，而非真的买命。
annotations.example: Are you offering help, or buying silence?

annotations.explain: swallow one's words/remark 是比喻，指忍住本想出口的话。
annotations.example: He swallowed his reply and nodded.

annotations.explain: far off 可指距离、时间或与合理预期相差很大；rather 在此是克制的语气。
annotations.example: Your estimate is far off the actual cost.

annotations.explain: speak one's mind 表示坦率表达真实想法，可能含夸赞也可能含责备。
annotations.example: She's never afraid to speak her mind.

annotations.explain: be willing to + 动词 强调意愿，和 can（能力）应区分。
annotations.example: Few buyers are willing to pay that much.

annotations.explain: work out 可指计算、想出办法或解决问题，依宾语和上下文判断。
annotations.example: We'll work out the details tomorrow.

annotations.explain: push back 有推回原位的字面义，也可指推迟或反驳；本句是字面动作。
annotations.example: She pushed the contract back across the table.

annotations.explain: would 在条件句主句里表示假设结果，用来礼貌地提出请求。
annotations.example: We'd be grateful if you could help.

annotations.explain: let's say 在这里不是提出数学假设，而是用委婉、带刺的方式结束谈判。
annotations.example: Let's say we never discussed it.

annotations.explain: ask about 指询问某项信息，不等于正式出价。
annotations.example: Someone called asking about the price.

annotations.explain: besides 表示“除……之外还包括”，区别于 except（排除在外）。
annotations.example: Besides Sarah, two others came.

annotations.explain: one's smile froze 是常见叙事描写，表现突发惊讶、恐惧或尴尬。
annotations.example: His smile froze when he saw the bill.

annotations.explain: hold out 可指在困难条件下坚持、支撑，也可指等待更好的条件。
annotations.example: How long can the business hold out?

annotations.explain: salvage 可用于挽救关系、合同、局面，不仅指打捞沉船。
annotations.example: They tried to salvage the partnership.

annotations.phrase: why make an enemy of them
annotations.explain: make an enemy of somebody 是固定搭配，表示把某人变成敌人。
annotations.example: Don't make an enemy of the only ally you have.

annotations.explain: that's what ... is/was about 用于揭示背后目的或真正问题。
annotations.example: Now I see what this argument is about.

annotations.explain: glance at 是短暂看一眼；stare at 强调持续盯着看。
annotations.example: She glanced at the clock.

annotations.explain: slide 在这里指让纸张沿桌面滑动，常比 push 更轻、更克制。
annotations.example: He slid the folder toward me.

annotations.explain: fall behind on payments/dues/work 是常见搭配；这里指会费没有拖欠。
annotations.example: We fell behind on the rent.

annotations.explain: dues 指组织成员定期缴纳的费用；与 debt 不完全相同。
annotations.example: Members must pay their annual dues.

annotations.explain: endorsement 在此是书面签字认可某些事实，不能理解为政府放行许可。
annotations.example: We need an endorsement confirming the dates.

annotations.explain: on someone's behalf 表示代替、代表其行事，常见于商务与正式交往。
annotations.example: I'm speaking on behalf of the team.

annotations.explain: if that's inconvenient 是礼貌但坚决的谈判退路，不是在恳求对方通融。
annotations.example: If that's inconvenient, we'll ask elsewhere.

annotations.explain: go + 形容词可表示状态变化，如 go quiet/pale/still。
annotations.example: The room went still.

annotations.explain: chime in 指适时加入谈话，语气通常不如 interrupt 生硬。
annotations.example: Her sister chimed in with an example.

annotations.explain: count for something 是固定表达，表示某事具有价值或分量。
annotations.example: Experience must count for something.

annotations.explain: fall silent 是描写气氛变化的惯用搭配，比 become silent 更自然凝练。
annotations.example: The crowd fell silent.

annotations.explain: verify 指通过证据核实，并不等于凭感觉相信；myself 加强责任边界。
annotations.example: I verified the figure myself.

annotations.explain: find + 宾语 可表达设法取得所需资源或人选，强调实际安排。
annotations.example: We'll find another witness.

annotations.explain: put one's name to something 指签署、具名支持，强调要为内容负责。
annotations.example: Don't put your name to a false claim.

annotations.explain: stand behind one's words/work 表示愿意为言论或成果担责，不是站在物体后面。
annotations.example: I stand behind every word of the report.

annotations.explain: be satisfied with 表示满意于结果；这里省略 with，强调反应。
annotations.example: She wasn't satisfied with the answer.

annotations.explain: rap 在这里是用扇子等物轻敲，和音乐风格 rap 无关。
annotations.example: He rapped on the door twice.

annotations.explain: be about to do 表示动作即将发生，常与 was/were 连用描写被打断的行为。
annotations.example: I was about to leave when she called.

annotations.explain: tear ... off ... 表示用力扯下、拆下；这里用荒诞比较嘲讽出价过低。
annotations.example: He tore the label off the bottle.

annotations.explain: all the more reason (to do something) 是常见强调句，用理由反推更该怎么做。
annotations.example: That's all the more reason to check.

annotations.explain: tuck something away 表示仔细收起来，通常放进安全、不显眼的位置。
annotations.example: She tucked the note away in her pocket.

annotations.explain: X-by-X 是构词模式，强调一个接一个分别处理：step-by-step, case-by-case。
annotations.example: We'll review the cases one by one.

annotations.explain: overturn 可指物理推翻，也可指推翻决定；本句借极端动作比喻谈判失控。
annotations.example: He almost overturned the chair.

annotations.explain: wouldn't have 与 if you'd ... 构成对过去的非真实假设，强调差点失去成果。
annotations.example: Without her help, we wouldn't have finished.

annotations.explain: 过去进行时可表示认知逐渐变化，而不是瞬间完全理解。
annotations.example: I was beginning to see her point.

annotations.explain: in one sitting 表示不间断一次完成，常用于阅读、写作或谈判。
annotations.example: She read the book in one sitting.

annotations.explain: take advantage of 在负面语境指利用对方弱势或信任；有时也可中性指利用机会。
annotations.example: Don't let them take advantage of you.

annotations.explain: by the time 强调一个较晚时间点到来之前，另一事件已完成；常与完成时搭配。
annotations.example: By the time I arrived, they had left.

annotations.explain: whether 引导名词性从句，表示两种可能未定，不可直接译为“是否肯定”。
annotations.example: We don't know whether it will work.

annotations.explain: gamble on + 名词/动名词表示冒险押注于某结果，常含风险和不确定性。
annotations.example: Don't gamble on a last-minute delivery.

annotations.phrase: didn't so much as raise an eyebrow
annotations.explain: not so much as ... 表示“连最小反应也没有”；raise an eyebrow 常表示惊讶。
annotations.example: She didn't so much as blink.

annotations.explain: 比较级 + than I expected 是高频说法，even 增强出乎预料的程度。
annotations.example: The price was even lower than I expected.

annotations.explain: try something like that 可指使用某种手段或做法，具体褒贬靠上下文。
annotations.example: I never thought he'd try that.

annotations.phrase: how low he'd dare to go
annotations.explain: how + 形容词 + 主语 + 动词 是嵌入式间接疑问结构；dare to 突出胆量。
annotations.example: I wonder how far they'd dare to go.

annotations.explain: charge + 金额或费率 表示收取费用，这里是李氏务实地决定提高报价。
annotations.example: The firm charges a higher rate for rush work.

annotations.explain: it strikes somebody that ... 是高频表达，表示某个想法突然浮现。
annotations.example: It struck me that we were late.

annotations.phrase: picked the wrong family to bully
annotations.explain: pick the wrong person/family to ... 带口语警告意味，强调对方低估了目标。
annotations.example: You picked the wrong person to threaten.

annotations.explain: halfway through + 名词或 doing 表示一件事进行到一半时。
annotations.example: Halfway through dinner, the phone rang.

annotations.explain: a few days ago 表示从现在往前数几天；区别于 yesterday，修正跨章节时间线。
annotations.example: We met a few days ago.

annotations.phrase: wasn't sure I wanted to ask
annotations.explain: wasn't sure I wanted to ... 通过犹豫的间接表达体现害怕知道答案。
annotations.example: I wasn't sure I wanted to hear it.

annotations.explain: marked + 文字/记号是过去分词短语，后置修饰 entry。
annotations.example: Find the box marked urgent.

annotations.explain: stop doing 表示停止原本动作；stop to do 表示停下另一事去做某事。
annotations.example: She stopped writing and looked up.

annotations.explain: Only when 引导的时间状语位于句首，主句常发生倒装：Only when ... did she ...。
annotations.example: Only when he left did she relax.

annotations.phrase: the two of us were alone
annotations.explain: the two of us 指我们两个人，were alone 表示没有其他人在场。
annotations.example: The two of us were alone in the room.

annotations.explain: 独立的名词 + 过去分词结构补充描写纸的状态：its folds (were) worn white。
annotations.example: The coat hung there, its sleeves worn thin.

annotations.phrase: had someone bring it to me
annotations.explain: have + 人 + 动词原形 表示安排或让某人做某事；不是完成时。
annotations.example: She had her assistant call me.

annotations.explain: oversee 意为监督、统筹，和 personally transport 不同。
annotations.example: He oversees the logistics team.

annotations.explain: 过去完成时 had entered 表示记账动作早于眼前检查单据这一过去时点。
annotations.example: She had recorded the payment earlier.

annotations.explain: beside 表示空间上的“在旁边”，区别于 besides（此外）。
annotations.example: The date was written beside the name.

annotations.explain: want + 宾语 + to do 是常见复合宾语结构；issue 在这里表示正式开出文书。
annotations.example: They wanted us to issue a receipt.

annotations.explain: state that ... 表示正式陈述某事实或主张，不等于已被证实。
annotations.example: The letter states that payment was made.

annotations.explain: entire 强调整体、没有缺漏，用于证据的精确表述尤其重要。
annotations.example: The entire shipment was delayed.

annotations.explain: 一般过去时询问过去实际是否发生，区别于反事实的 would you have changed it。
annotations.example: Did you sign the form?

annotations.explain: at once 表示立刻、毫不迟疑，比 soon 更及时。
annotations.example: She answered at once.

annotations.explain: but 构成两件可同时成立但道德性质不同的事：没造假，不代表没收钱。
annotations.example: I didn't sign it, but I kept the payment.

annotations.explain: go blank 描写瞬间不知道如何反应，也可形容记忆突然想不起来。
annotations.example: My mind went blank during the test.

annotations.explain: should have + 过去分词 表示对已经发生的过去行为作批评或遗憾判断。
annotations.example: You should have told me earlier.

annotations.explain: at the time 用于回顾过去背景或当年的认知，与现在的判断形成对照。
annotations.example: At the time, I thought it was safe.

annotations.explain: stop + doing 表示停止持续的行为；harass 通常指持续滋扰、施压。
annotations.example: They must stop harassing the workers.

annotations.explain: report something to somebody 既可指向上级报告，也可指向警方或官府告发。
annotations.example: She reported the incident to the police.

annotations.explain: 现在完成时强调从过去延续到说话时点的状态；与 ever since 连用自然。
annotations.example: The money has remained untouched.

annotations.explain: not a single + 单数名词 是强调完全没有的常见结构。
annotations.example: Not a single page was missing.

annotations.explain: 现在分词 gripping 后置修饰 fingers，等于 fingers that were gripping ...。
annotations.example: The man holding the box was nervous.

annotations.explain: go + 形容词表示状态变化，had gone white 通过身体细节显露紧张。
annotations.example: Her knuckles had gone white.

annotations.explain: meet someone's eyes/gaze 表示与人目光相接，具有面对问题的意味。
annotations.example: She met his eyes without flinching.

annotations.explain: intend to do 表示计划或意图，不等于已经实施。
annotations.example: They intended to file a complaint.

annotations.explain: fail to do 可表示未做到某事，不必理解成主观忘记；这里涉及道德责任。
annotations.example: He failed to disclose the payment.

annotations.explain: speak out 指公开发表意见、揭露不公，比简单 speak 更有立场。
annotations.example: She finally spoke out about the issue.

annotations.explain: blameless 指没有责任或过失，不等同于法律意义“无罪”的正式裁决。
annotations.example: No one in the dispute was entirely blameless.

annotations.explain: had been trying to 描写当时持续的努力；only 带出想替母亲辩解的主观倾向。
annotations.example: She had only been trying to help.

annotations.phrase: the words died on my lips
annotations.meaning: 话到了嘴边却说不出口
annotations.explain: words die on someone's lips 是文学惯用描写，表示原本想说的话突然停住。
annotations.example: The apology died on his lips.

annotations.explain: 被动语态强调粮食遭到转移，故意不指定实施者，保持证据边界。
annotations.example: The supplies had been taken away.

annotations.explain: count on somebody/something 表示依靠、指望，是常见短语动词。
annotations.example: Families were counting on the aid.

annotations.explain: survive + 时间/灾难 表示挺过困难时期，语义比 live through 更突出风险。
annotations.example: The village struggled to survive the winter.

annotations.phrase: too hot for anyone to touch
annotations.explain: too + 形容词 + for sb to do 是常见程度结果结构，既可字面也可比喻。
annotations.example: The topic was too sensitive to discuss.

annotations.phrase: Not from me, at any rate
annotations.explain: at any rate 表示“至少在这一点上”“无论如何”，语境中限制陈述范围。
annotations.example: At any rate, I didn't approve the plan.

annotations.explain: be supposed to 表达预期职责或被要求做什么，在疑问句中可显出无助。
annotations.example: What am I supposed to say?

annotations.explain: toward 表示动作方向；不同于 to 强调最终到达。
annotations.example: She pushed the cup toward him.

annotations.explain: deserve to do/know 常体现道德或情理上的应得，而非法律定义。
annotations.example: They deserve to know the truth.

annotations.explain: give an account of sth 是正式说法，意思为交代经过；account 在这里不是银行账户。
annotations.example: He gave a full account of the incident.

annotations.explain: along with 是高频介词短语，表示随同、连带。
annotations.example: Send the invoice along with the form.

annotations.explain: whether ... or ... 表示两种可能都包括，强调不回避后果。
annotations.example: Whether we win or lose, we'll continue.

annotations.explain: use something against somebody 表示利用某信息、证据或弱点攻击对方。
annotations.example: Don't let them use your words against you.

annotations.phrase: looked from the receipt to her face
annotations.explain: look from A to B 是视线转换，常用于表现心情复杂、难以开口。
annotations.example: He looked from the letter to the door.

annotations.explain: have no intention of doing 是固定表达，后接动名词，不接 to do。
annotations.example: They have no intention of apologizing.

annotations.explain: live in peace 强调免于骚扰、冲突的安宁状态。
annotations.example: We just want to live in peace.

annotations.phrase: giving them a handhold on my throat
annotations.explain: handhold 原指攀爬时可抓住的地方；此处比喻把柄使别人能钳制自己。
annotations.example: Don't give them a way to control you.

annotations.explain: hand something back 是递还原物的高频短语动词。
annotations.example: She handed the keys back.

annotations.explain: go with sb 强调同行；不一定有“同意某观点”的意思。
annotations.example: I'll go with you to the office.

annotations.explain: be going to 表示预期或打算；scold 比 blame 更侧重当面训斥。
annotations.example: Are you going to scold me for this?

annotations.explain: do some/any good 是常见习语，表示带来作用或好处；反问暗示未必有效。
annotations.example: Would arguing do any good?

annotations.explain: every now and then 表示时不时、偶尔，与 all the time 不同。
annotations.example: We meet for coffee every now and then.

annotations.explain: keep + doing 表示持续或反复做某事；和 keep to do 不一样。
annotations.example: He kept asking questions.

annotations.explain: manage to do 通常指费力终于做到；否定式表示没有办法完成某个反应。
annotations.example: I couldn't manage a smile.

annotations.explain: reach out 表示伸出手，也可抽象表示主动联系；这里取字面义。
annotations.example: She reached out and held his hand.

annotations.explain: stiffen 表示身体因紧张或惊讶突然僵硬；for a moment 指持续很短。
annotations.example: He stiffened at the accusation.

annotations.explain: that's enough + 名词/doing 是口语中温和或不耐烦地叫停某事。
annotations.example: That's enough joking for today.

annotations.explain: as usual 是惯用副词短语，表示行为符合某人的一贯模式。
annotations.example: She arrived early as usual.

annotations.phrase: some of the tension had finally left her voice
annotations.explain: 将 tension 拟人化为“离开声音”，属于常见含蓄的情绪描写。
annotations.example: The anger slowly left his voice.

annotations.explain: for the first time 表示此前从未出现的变化；that night 将时间限定在当晚。
annotations.example: For the first time, she felt hopeful.

annotations.explain: 过去进行时描述当时脑中的持续状态，和瞬间想到的 thought of 不同。
annotations.example: I wasn't thinking about the exam.

annotations.phrase: Only one thought filled my head
annotations.explain: only 放句首限定唯一内容，fill one's head/mind 表示念头占据全部注意力。
annotations.example: One question filled my mind.

annotations.phrase: how was I supposed to tell
annotations.explain: how was I supposed to ... 是带焦虑或无奈的反问，比 how could I 更强调职责压力。
annotations.example: How was I supposed to explain that?

scenes.title: 黎明姜府议事
scenes.alt: 天未亮的姜府前院里，李氏主持掌柜与伙计议事，桌上摆着算盘、货样和文书，姜明月与春桃在旁。

scenes.title: 契书提前催还
scenes.alt: 李氏指着借款契书上的小字向姜明月说明提前催还的风险，秦叔在旁记录。

scenes.title: 蒋会首压价
scenes.alt: 海棠花下的会谈桌旁，蒋会首递出铺面转让草约，姜明月与二姑母、秦叔对坐周旋。

scenes.title: 争取有限签注
scenes.alt: 商谈结束后，秦叔收好只就亲历部分签署的签注，姜明月与二姑母在旁。

scenes.title: 姜家未停生意
scenes.alt: 傍晚的账房与货场中，李氏审阅回执、秦叔汇报调度，危机里商号仍在运转。

scenes.title: 两百两存单
scenes.alt: 静室烛影里，李氏取出折痕发白的旧存单向姜明月坦白，室内只有母女二人。

scenes.title: 母女拥抱
scenes.alt: 昏暖灯下，姜明月抱住李氏，李氏略僵硬后轻抚她后背，情绪克制而温柔。
